task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 -- IMPLEMENT the gate-approved fix design for ISS-0109 (GH#358).

THE DESIGN IS AUTHORITATIVE: lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md. It passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's gate at commit
bf87afb (re-gate PASS, handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-02b-code-design-validator.json), plus two
invariant-label corrections ORCH applied directly afterwards. Implement what it specifies
-- do not redesign it, and do not "improve" a contract it settled. If you find something
in it that is genuinely wrong or unbuildable, STOP and report it as a BLOCKER in
result.issues rather than deviating silently; the design has already been through a gate
that re-derived its claims from source, so a disagreement is worth surfacing, not
absorbing.

CONTEXT YOU NEED, so you do not re-derive it (full reasoning in
handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json):
- ISS-0109's OWN stated mechanism was refuted. The tenant schema was NOT dropped out from
  under a live test; the logged DROP/DELETE/DELETE triple is the failing test's own
  post-failure on_exit teardown. The real fault class is provisioning/replay completeness.
- There is NO production defect. lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex and
  lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex are NOT to be modified (INV-F-2, SS2.3).
  This run is TEST-SIDE ONLY. If your diff touches lib/ for any reason other than the
  design artefact itself, that is a signal you have gone off-design -- stop and report it.
- Ecto's Migrator re-applies nothing for an already-recorded version. This was measured,
  not assumed: after dropping promotion_assertion_runs while leaving version
  20260818090001 recorded, a second replay_migrations/1 returned {:ok, []} with the table
  still absent. That measurement is WHY the completeness assertion has to check the table
  oracle and not just replay's return value.

WHAT TO BUILD, per the design:
1. test/support/tenant_fixture.ex -- a new test-only module Letflow.TenantFixture, plain
   module (not a GenServer, never in the supervision tree, never referenced from lib/) with
   the four public functions and full @specs the design specifies: the provisioning entry
   point, capture_schema_state/1, assert_schema_complete!/2, and expected_tenant_tables/0.
   SS3.5 is NORMATIVE for capture_schema_state/1's failure boundary and the invariant table's
   INV-F-4 row explicitly defers to it: a single failing query is ALWAYS a per-field
   degradation returning {:ok, schema_state()}; {:error, {:capture_failed, _}} is only the
   outer net for a failure outside the per-field guards. Get the degradation rule right --
   if tables_present degrades to [], tables_missing must ALSO be [], never "all 19 missing".
   Reporting an unobserved set as an observed absence would make the capture actively
   misleading, which is worse than not having it.
2. The teardown log line: exactly ONE line before the DROP, carrying the literal marker
   LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE and the closed phase vocabulary
   (teardown | provision_failed | replay_failed | incomplete_schema) plus
   schema_present_before_drop. The whole point is that a teardown line is structurally
   impossible to mistake for a mid-test drop -- that ambiguity is what produced ISS-0109's
   original misdiagnosis.
   OQ-4 FROM THE DESIGN, YOU MUST SETTLE IT: if the configured log level filters :info, this
   line silently vanishes and scope item (B) is defeated. Check the actual configured level
   (config/test.exs and any runtime override). If :info is filtered, raise THIS ONE LINE to
   :warning -- do NOT reconfigure the logger to make :info visible. That would be satisfying
   a gate by changing what it measures, and it would alter output for every other test.
   Report which you found and what you did.
3. Adoption in EXACTLY TWO modules: test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs and
   test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs. The other 39 copy-paste
   sites are ISS-0112/GH#366 and are OUT OF SCOPE -- do not touch them.
   Note drop_schema!/1 STAYS in promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs: it has a second,
   unrelated SandboxPool caller at :463 (verified by the gate). Deleting it would break that.
4. Do NOT write the regression tests. TEST-DESIGNER owns Step 4 and will build them from the
   design's FAIL-FIRST section. Your job is the helper and the adoption.

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVATION EVIDENCE (SS7.7 -- this is the one deliverable with no fail-first
proof, so its evidence is a before/after comparison and you are the one who can capture the
"before"): BEFORE editing either module, run both of them and record the real output. Then
adopt the helper and run them again. Both runs' actual output goes in result.summary. A
refactor claimed to be behaviour-preserving without a before-run is not evidence, it is an
assertion.

VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING (No Speculation -- quote real output, never "should pass"):
- Plain `mix compile` (NOT --warnings-as-errors: main itself fails that under this host's
  Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 vs the 1.18.3-otp-27 pin, ISS-0106/GH#354, already filed and not
  yours). Your NEW code must still add no warnings of its own -- read the compile output and
  say so.
- The two adopted modules, before and after, as above.
- Do NOT run `mix format --check-formatted` against the tree (same ISS-0106 skew). Formatting
  your own new file with `mix format` on THIS toolchain would introduce 1.20-formatter drift
  into a repo pinned to 1.18.3 -- so hand-match the surrounding style instead and say that
  you did.
- `mix` may not be on PATH bare; invoke "/c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix" quoted if needed.
  Postgres for this workspace is on LETFLOW_DB_PORT from ./.env (5472), its own container.

Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821. Commit by explicit filename, never `git add -A`.
acceptance_criteria: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex exists and implements Letflow.TenantFixture exactly as the gate-approved design specifies: the four public functions with @specs, test-only, not a GenServer, not in the supervision tree, not referenced from lib/

capture_schema_state/1 implements SS3.5's nested failure boundary: a single failing query degrades that field and still returns {:ok, schema_state()}; {:error, {:capture_failed, _}} occurs only outside the per-field guards; a degraded tables_present yields tables_missing == [] rather than a false 'all missing', and the same rule holds for applied_versions/versions_missing
Exactly one teardown log line is emitted before the DROP, carrying the literal LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE marker, a phase from the closed vocabulary, and schema_present_before_drop

OQ-4 is settled with evidence: the configured test log level was checked, and the line is emitted at a level that is actually visible -- raising this one line to :warning if :info is filtered, WITHOUT reconfiguring the logger

The helper is adopted in exactly test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs and test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs; no other test file is modified; drop_schema!/1 remains in promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs for its unrelated SandboxPool caller at :463
lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex are unmodified (INV-F-2), and git diff shows no lib/ change other than the design artefact
No regression tests were written (TEST-DESIGNER owns Step 4)

Real quoted output is given for: plain mix compile (with a statement about whether the new code adds warnings), and BOTH adopted modules run BEFORE adoption and AFTER adoption, as SS7.7's behaviour-preservation evidence
